proposal.summary: An attacker can gain write access to a read-only ashmem mapping by using remap_file_pages() to invoke the backing shmem file's ->mmap() handler (which is stored in vm_file) and thereby set VM_MAYWRITE, allowing mprotect() to make the mapping writable. Additionally, ashmem allows marking pages purgable (ASHMEM_UNPIN/ASHMEM_PIN) without requiring write permissions.
proposal.affected_product: Android ashmem kernel driver (kernel staging/android/ashmem.c) and any users of ashmem (e.g. Chrome, art JIT usage); tested on upstream Linux and Pixel 2 (security patch level 2019-09-05)
proposal.cwe_quote:
However, it improperly stores the backing shmem file, whose ->mmap() handler
does not enforce the same restrictions, in ->vm_file.

AV.quote:
remap_file_pages(addr, size, 0, 0, 0) on an ashmem mapping allows an
attacker to raise the VM_MAYWRITE bit, allowing the attacker to gain write
access to the ashmem allocation's backing file via mprotect().

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify kernel versions/patch level where ashmem's mmap stores vm_file and whether remap_file_pages is permitted by platform seccomp; reproduce locally and backport a fix that avoids setting vma->vm_file to the backing shmem file (or ensure the backing file's ->mmap enforces the same prot_mask), and restrict remap_file_pages syscall where not needed.

evidence_quotes.claim: ashmem stores backing shmem file in vm_file
evidence_quotes.quote:
However, it improperly stores the backing shmem file, whose ->mmap() handler
does not enforce the same restrictions, in ->vm_file.

evidence_quotes.claim: remap_file_pages can be used to call mmap handler creating new VMA
evidence_quotes.quote:
An attacker can abuse this through the remap_file_pages() syscall, which grabs the file pointer of an
existing VMA and calls its ->mmap() handler to create a new VMA.

evidence_quotes.claim: remap_file_pages attack raises VM_MAYWRITE allowing mprotect to make mapping writable
evidence_quotes.quote:
In effect,
calling remap_file_pages(addr, size, 0, 0, 0) on an ashmem mapping allows an
attacker to raise the VM_MAYWRITE bit, allowing the attacker to gain write
access to the ashmem allocation's backing file via mprotect().

evidence_quotes.claim: ashmem purgable pages can be marked without write access
evidence_quotes.quote:
